# Canonical test corpus

A minimal, self-generated corpus of DWG files that CI runs
`coverage_report` against (task #94). Five files, one per DWG version
the write path can assemble.

| File                  | Version        | Container   | Records | decoded / skip / err | ratio |
|-----------------------|----------------|-------------|----------|----------------------|-------|
| `synthetic_2000.dwg`  | AC1015 (R2000) | flat §3.2.6 | 11       | 11 / 0 / 0           | 100 % |
| `synthetic_2004.dwg`  | AC1018 (R2004) | page map §4 | 11       | 11 / 0 / 0           | 100 % |
| `synthetic_2010.dwg`  | AC1024 (R2010) | page map §4 | 11       | 11 / 0 / 0           | 100 % |
| `synthetic_2013.dwg`  | AC1027 (R2013) | page map §4 | 11       | 11 / 0 / 0           | 100 % |
| `synthetic_2018.dwg`  | AC1032 (R2018) | page map §4 | 11       | 11 / 0 / 0           | 100 % |
| **TOTAL**             |                |             | 55       | 55 / 0 / 0           | 100 % |

Each file carries the same eleven records: five entities (a 2D LINE, a 3D
LINE with non-default thickness and extrusion, a CIRCLE, an ARC, and a
POINT) and three block definitions, a BLOCK_HEADER table entry plus the
BLOCK sentinel it names, six records in all (#78). The blocks are
`FixtureBlock`, whose header and sentinel store the same name, and two
anonymous blocks whose headers both store the stem `*D` and whose
sentinels read `*D1` and `*D2`, so the name join of
`dwg::graph::resolve_block_names` (#70) has work to do on every release the
writer emits. Each header's handle stream holds the block control object
(soft pointer, not in the file), the NULL anchor and its BLOCK; the
references after the BLOCK (entities, ENDBLK, layout) are left out.

The R2004-family files carry three sections — `AcDb:Header` (64 zero
bytes, placeholder), `AcDb:Handles`, `AcDb:AcDbObjects` — assembled by
`assemble_dwg_bytes`. `synthetic_2000.dwg` has no section map at all:
§3.2.6 gives R13-R15 a flat list of `(record number, absolute seeker,
size)` locators, the object records sit loose in the file, and the
object map addresses them by absolute file offset. That is what makes
it a *different* gate rather than a fifth copy of the same one — it is
the only fixture whose handle-map offsets are file offsets.

Every integrity field in it is real: the §3.2 file-header CRC and
end sentinel (#214), the §9 header-variable and §10.1 class sections'
sentinels, sizes and CRCs, and the §23.1 object-map and §20.1 record
CRCs (#216). CI walks it with the strict
streaming container reader. What remains placeholder is content: the
header variables are 26 zero bytes, the class table is empty, and no
AutoCAD build has opened the file. The R2004-family files share the
object-map and record CRCs but are not walked by the streaming reader.

The R2004-family file headers carry the §4.1 fixed fields every real
R2004, R2010, R2013 and R2018 file checked has: the long `0x80` at 0x28,
the decrypted block's `0x6C`, `4`, `1`, `0x20`, `0x80` and `0x40` at
0x10, 0x14, 0x24, 0x44, 0x48 and 0x4C, and the magic sequence continued
to 0x100 in the 0x14 bytes after the block. Their system pages (§4.3) and
data page headers (§4.6) carry the §4.2 page checksums real files carry,
at the spec's offsets (#265). They still have no second
header copy at the end of the file (its address is 0), and their LZ77
streams end at `0x11` with unpadded data pages, unlike AutoCAD's (#163).

## Licence and provenance

**Apache-2.0, same as the rest of this repository.** These files are
generated byte-for-byte by code in this repository; not one byte
originates from an Autodesk-, Open-Design-Alliance-, or other
third-party-produced DWG. Nothing here is vendored, and no external
corpus is redistributed. This is why the corpus can be committed at
all — the obvious external candidate (`nextgis/dwg_samples`) declares
no licence, so its contents are not redistributable.

Generator: [`examples/build_fixtures.rs`](../../../examples/build_fixtures.rs),
driving `dwg::file_writer::assemble_dwg_bytes` (write-path Stages 1-5),
`dwg::handle_map::write_handle_map`, and the
`dwg::element_encoder::ElementEncoder` entity encoders. The R2000
fixture uses `build_flat_fixture` in the same example instead of
`assemble_dwg_bytes`, which does not accept the flat layout.

Command line:

```sh
cargo run --release --example build_fixtures
```

First generated on top of `main` at commit `075f3fe`
("deps(deps): bump the patch-updates group across 1 directory with 4
updates (#11)"), with `examples/build_fixtures.rs` added in the same
change that committed these files.

Generation is byte-deterministic: re-running the command on an
unchanged tree leaves `git status` clean. If a future change to the
writer, the LZ77 encoder, the handle-map writer, or the entity
encoders legitimately alters the output, regenerate and commit the new
bytes in the same PR — the diff is the evidence that the change was
intentional.

## Honest scope

These fixtures prove **our reader round-trips our writer**. They are
not evidence that AutoCAD, BricsCAD, or LibreCAD accept the bytes; see
the acceptance statement in `src/file_writer.rs`. CI does not run any
Autodesk product.

Coverage is limited to the four entity types that currently have an
`ElementEncoder` implementation (LINE, CIRCLE, ARC, POINT) and the
block records, which the generator writes by hand, inverting
`tables::block_record` and `entities::block` (no `ElementEncoder` exists
for them). Add fixtures as more encoders land — every new encoder is a
chance to widen this gate.

No R14 or R2007 fixture exists. R14 entity records need the §20.4.1
R13/R14 preamble and the §20.4.21 `3BD` LINE body, which the
`ElementEncoder` implementations do not write; R2007's §5.1-§5.4
container is implemented read-only, and writing one would need a
Reed-Solomon encoder and a §5.10 compressor this crate does not have.
Both releases are covered on the read side by the real corpus and by
`tests/integration_legacy_container.rs`, whose R14 fixtures are built
byte-by-byte in the test itself.

## What CI does with this

`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, job **Coverage smoke test (canonical
corpus)**:

- fails outright if this directory holds no `.dwg` file (the job used
  to skip with a warning, which made it a vacuous gate),
- runs `cargo run --release --example coverage_report -- tests/fixtures/canonical`,
- parses the aggregate `ratio%` off the `TOTAL` row and fails below the
  threshold stated in the workflow.

The tight companion gate is [`tests/canonical_corpus.rs`](../../canonical_corpus.rs),
which runs under `cargo test` and pins the exact per-file record counts
*and* decoded field values — so a bit-alignment regression that still
"decodes" into garbage coordinates fails there even when the ratio
would stay at 100 %.

[`tests/block_names.rs`](../../block_names.rs) runs the block-name gate
(#70) on these five files, in `cargo test` on every platform (`ci.yml`, job
**Test**, step `cargo test --release`, as `canonical_fixtures_block_names_agree_with_their_sentinels`):
each BLOCK_HEADER's
resolved name must equal the name its BLOCK sentinel carries, the resolved
names must be unique, and the header's stored string must be that name
minus a decimal suffix. Until #78 the gate ran only where the public
corpus was present.

A regression that breaks the entity walker, the common-entity preamble,
LINE / CIRCLE / ARC / POINT decoding, the section map, or the handle
map trips one or both guards.
